verdict.world: B (dominant); world A and world C rejected
verdict.world_A_never_learned_gate: REJECTED — full-QK reaches the Bayes floor (0.2434 vs 0.2416); gate is performed, captures 87% of the gating value (0.2556-0.2434)/(0.2556-0.2416).
verdict.world_C_h22_formula_off: REJECTED — h22 surrogate 0.0189 is only ~1.35x the exact gating value 0.0140 (and ~2x the affine-lag gap 0.0095); formula basically correct.
verdict.world_B_posonly_exceeds_theorem_class: CONFIRMED and dominant — pos-only+LN (0.2447) beats the affine lag-only frontier (0.2511) and nearly reaches Bayes; linearizing LayerNorm returns it to the frontier (0.2503). LayerNorm's content-dependent normalization smuggles the parent->child gate into a content-blind-pattern model.
verdict.h21_null_claim_correction: The affine-lag class does NOT pay zero on the null control under occlusion (0.073 occ / 0.028 clean) because optimal filtering of any partially-observed chain is nonlinear; the pure gating value must be measured against parent-blind Bayes (=0 on null), not the affine class.
verdict.h31_caveat: The FRA-QK cut-worth is redundant with LayerNorm (~78% of the gate is LN-recoverable), so cut(Q-hat) measures ~0.0013 not Delta_gate=0.014; measure the H4 QK cut against a LN-free/linearized-LN content-blind baseline (expect ~0.006).

one_sentence: The rung-1 14x shortfall is a LayerNorm measurement confound, not a theory error: H2.2's gating value (0.0189) closely tracks the exact gate (Bayes vs parent-blind = 0.0140) and the full model reaches the Bayes floor, but the tiny empirical full-minus-position-only gap (0.0013) collapses because LayerNorm's content-dependent normalization lets the position-only model approximate the gate (0.2447, below the analytic lag-only frontier 0.2511) and linearizing it returns the model to the frontier (0.2503) -- world B.
